thread:
Maria: Following up on the RFC: propose we treat capabilities as first-class in deployment manifests (capability-first). The runtime picks a strategy from the capability vector instead of hardcoding hosted/dedicated/private branches.
Kevin: Hmm. How do we avoid combinatorial explosion of adapters if every runtime combines capabilities differently?
Maria: The runtime implements a small set of canonical execution strategies (fast-path, secure-path, isolated-path, fallback-path). Each strategy declares which capabilities it requires; the capability registry picks the best-fit strategy.
Jasper: We need strict rules for when strategy switching is allowed. No mid-request model swap; only choose strategy at request start. Otherwise tracing/billing gets messy.
Anya: Security constraint: any strategy that uses customer-managed keys must present an attestation token. For private/on-prem we allow long-lived attestations minted at deploy time.
Kevin: Billing/telemetry idea: emit a capability_meter tag per request with the chosen strategy and capability_flags. Ops can synthesize cost from that.
Jasper: Also track fallback_reason when preferred capability not available (e.g., kv-cache-miss, no-burst-capacity). Metric = fallback_count / total_requests.
Maria: Proposed manifest example (capabilities + intent + downgrade policy):

```json
{
  "deployment": "acme-search-001",
  "model": "redwood-gpt-2b",
  "intent": "llm-embed-and-rewrite",
  "capabilities": [
    { "name": "low-latency", "policy": "preferred" },
    { "name": "kv-cache", "policy": "best-effort" },
    { "name": "kms-ekm", "policy": "required" },
    { "name": "gpu-quant", "policy": "preferred" }
  ]
}
```

Anya: Nice. For kms-ekm==required we reject deploys without the attestation chain. For hosted mode we mint ephemeral EKM tokens scoped to tenant. For private we validate local attestation blob.
Kevin: Deployment lifecycle: 1) registry evaluate and suggest strategy. 2) runtime opts-in via feature flag. 3) phased enforcement. Keep billing path unchanged in phase 1/2.
Jasper: Migration specifics: add a header in existing traffic that records proposed_strategy but still route to legacy adapters. Compare latency and cost in staging before flipping.
Maria: Decision questions: should we allow strategies to be compositionally combined? e.g., low-latency + burstable becomes low-latency-burst strategy. I lean yes but runtime should cap complexity to N precompiled strategies.
Kevin: Agree. Limit to ~6 canonical strategies to keep testing tractable. Any more and rollout and perf matrices explode.
Anya: Audit/logging: every capability use must include key_id/attestor_id and control_plane_request_id. This must appear in tenant logs for compliance.
Jasper: Ops tasks: - add capability_meter label, - fallback_count alert, - per-tenant required_capability_violation alert.
Maria: Runtime implement checklist: capability registry client (cached), strategy matcher, attestation verifier, token fetcher, metrics hook. Try to keep registry client <1ms p99 lookup.
Kevin: Edge-case: what if runtime finds required capability missing mid-deploy due to degraded host? For required => fail fast; mark deployment degraded and emit incident.
Anya: For private mode with intermittent control plane, allow offline attestations and local policy cache with TTL. Must provide a revocation path (rebind on reconnect).
Jasper: Can we gate enforcement on tenant plan? e.g., enterprise tenants can require kms-ekm, others get preferred? Yes, control plane should allow capability overrides per-tenant.
Maria: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with sequence diagrams: control plane -> registry -> runtime decision -> attach capability_meter -> logs. Will include migration checklist.
Kevin: I can do a small runtime shim prototype to resolve strategy matching.
Jasper: Ops will wire the metrics and a quick Kibana dashboard.
